title: When the Confession Falls
premise: When a confession letter arrives at the office of coroner Ulyana Coldharbour—postmarked one day after the funeral of Judge Aldous Wren—she discovers it names her late father as an accomplice to a thirty-year-old death the town buried as an accident. As Ulyana reopens the case, she finds that half of Coldharbour's founding families built their fortunes on the silence, and that someone is willing to kill again before the statute expires in eleven days. Following alibis, falsified autopsy records, and her father's hidden ledger, Ulyana learns the confession was written by the victim's daughter, who has been living among them for years. In the end, Ulyana must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile peace her father died protecting—and she chooses truth, burning the town's old covenant even as it costs her the last person who still loved him.
about_author: P. M. Voss is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade handling estate files in towns where everyone knew everyone's business. They write mysteries about small places with long memories.

chapters.title: The Day After
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Two days after Judge Wren's funeral, Ulyana signs his burial permit and finds a confession letter slipped under her door, postmarked yesterday. It names her dead father in a thirty-year-old drowning ruled accidental. The beat: dread arriving on ordinary paperwork.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She walks the cemetery at dawn, checking the drowned girl's headstone against her father's old case notes. The dates don't align; the original autopsy was signed by a doctor who left town a week later. Beat: the first crack in seven years of tidy filing.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback to her father teaching her to file. She searches his effects and finds a locked ledger box missing from his study. Her mother, sharp-tongued and failing, warns her to let the dead stay dead. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain.

chapters.title: The Widow's Condolences
chapters.summary: Deputy Marshal Ivo Renner's POV. Ivo attends Wren's widow's reception and notices the guest list reads like the town charter—every founding family present, every alibi rehearsed. He spots Ulyana asking questions and decides to watch her. Beat: the machinery of respectability flexing.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A retired state attorney tells her the homicide statute expires in eleven days; after that, no court will ever touch it. Someone mailed the confession deliberately timed. Beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She dives the old quarry with a salvage friend and recovers a rusted satchel containing a girl's locket and a man's cufflink monogrammed A.W. The judge was there that night. Beat: grief curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo pulls thirty-year-old phone records and finds eleven calls made from the Wren house the night of the drowning—a call tree, someone organizing a story. His captain orders him off it. Beat: institutional rot revealed.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Records show Wren's daughter, Maren, supposedly sent abroad after the drowning—but a schoolteacher remembers a quiet girl who stayed, under another family's name. Beat: the confession's author may be closer than anyone thinks.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She finds the missing ledger box hidden in her father's boathouse: payments logged monthly for twenty-two years, initials only, stopping the month he died. Beat: her father was paid for silence—or paying it out.

chapters.title: A Polite Warning
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo's tires are slashed and a copy of the old accident report appears on his windshield, annotated: 'Signed and settled.' He realizes the town's elders are coordinating again. Beat: fear wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The widow Wren is found dead in her greenhouse, staged as a fall. Ulyana performs the autopsy and finds ligature marks under the bruising. Beat: the past has started killing in the present.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo goes around his captain to a state investigator, trading what he knows for protection he may not get. He and Ulyana form an uneasy alliance over bad coffee. Beat: two lonely people choosing each other's company.

chapters.title: Maren Hale
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She traces the alias to Maren Hale, now the town's beloved librarian, who has lived quietly among them for decades. Maren neither confirms nor denies writing the letter. Beat: sympathy for the ghost at the center of everything.

chapters.title: The Night at the Quarry
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, first time. Flashback: sixteen-year-old Maren watched her father and four men argue by the water; her mother went into the quarry and never came out; the town called it an accident and her father signed the paper. Beat: the wound shown whole.

chapters.title: Four Alibis
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Of the four surviving conspirators, three have airtight, mutually corroborating stories—too airtight, memorized like scripture. The fourth, old banker Corliss, has begun to ramble. Beat: the wall showing its seams.

chapters.title: Corliss Talks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dying Corliss confesses to Ulyana that her father wasn't a conspirator—he was blackmailing them to fund the girl's secret education, then planned to go public. They killed him for it and dressed it as a heart attack. Beat: the floor drops out of her inheritance.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Corliss dies hours later, and the state investigator's file vanishes; Ivo realizes the corruption reaches above the county. He chooses Ulyana over his badge. Beat: loyalty finally picking a side.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With the statute expiring, Ulyana reconstructs the chain of custody: the ledger, the quarry evidence, Corliss's recorded words—all of it inadmissible without a living witness. Only Maren can testify. Beat: everything balanced on one frightened woman.

chapters.title: The Library at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts Maren, who admits she wrote the confession—not for justice, but because she is dying and wanted one honest act. But she refuses to testify; the town raised her, fed her, hid her. Beat: mercy and fury in the same breath.

chapters.title: Coldharbour Rising
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The conspirators move on Maren; Ivo and Ulyana get her out through the cemetery as the town's remaining loyalists close ranks. A confrontation in the archive room ends with the ringleader, Councilman Vey, exposed before witnesses. Beat: climax—the truth dragged into daylight by force.

chapters.title: The Confession Falls
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the statute's final day, Maren testifies; Vey and two others are charged, and the sealed cases reopen. Ulyana files her father's true record alongside the lie, refusing to launder his memory. Beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: New Headstone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ulyana carves a corrected inscription for the drowned woman and shares coffee with Ivo as Maren, freed by truth, watches the river from the library steps. Beat: the price of survival paid, and worth it.
